content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the structure of carboxylic acids and identify the carboxyl group
Name and draw carboxylic acids with up to 4 carbon atoms
Describe the reactions of carboxylic acids with metals, bases, and carbonates
Explain why carboxylic acids are weak acids

are organic compounds containing the carboxyl functional group (-COOH). They are weak acids found in many natural substances - ethanoic acid in vinegar, citric acid in lemons, and amino acids in proteins.
The H in -COOH can dissociate to give H⁺
[DIAGRAM: Structure of carboxyl group showing C=O and -OH arrangement]
[DIAGRAM: Displayed formula of ethanoic acid showing all bonds]
Produce fewer H⁺ ions than strong acids
Have higher pH than strong acids of same concentration
Ethanoic acid + Magnesium → Magnesium ethanoate + Hydrogen
Ethanoic acid + Sodium hydroxide → Sodium ethanoate + Water
Ethanoic acid + Ethanol ⇌ Ethyl ethanoate + Water
Draw the displayed formula of propanoic acid.

H   H     O
    |   |     ‖
H — C — C — C — O — H
    |   |
    H   H
Write the equation for the reaction of ethanoic acid with sodium carbonate.
Products: Sodium ethanoate + Water + Carbon dioxide
Explain why ethanoic acid is a weak acid.
Ethanoic acid only partially dissociates in water
The dissociation equilibrium lies to the left:
Therefore, it has a higher pH than a strong acid of the same concentration
This makes it a weak acid
Compare the reactions of equal concentrations of hydrochloric acid and ethanoic acid with magnesium.
The same total amount of hydrogen is produced, but more slowly with the weak acid.
Thinking weak acids don't react with carbonates
Weak acids DO react, just more slowly
Weak = partially dissociates; dilute = low concentration
Write the molecular formula and structural formula of propanoic acid. (2 marks)
Write the equation for the reaction of methanoic acid with sodium hydroxide. (2 marks)
Describe and explain what you would observe when ethanoic acid is added to magnesium. (3 marks)
Explain what is meant by a 'weak acid'. (2 marks)
Compare the pH and reaction rate of 1 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid with 1 mol/dm³ ethanoic acid with magnesium. (4 marks)
Name the salt produced when butanoic acid reacts with calcium carbonate. (1 mark)

The splitting of a molecule into ions
The salt or ion formed from ethanoic acid
Methanoic acid, ethanoic acid, propanoic acid

With metals (→ salt + H₂), bases (→ salt + H₂O), carbonates (→ salt + H₂O + CO₂)
